demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson's two gates ask acme's golden rows, as lesson 11.2's gate did, and that gate judged its candidate with acme on the kit's own index: keep the pin for the duration, so every verdict on this page is about one lane, and put it back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: make smoke-deployed and make incident, line by line
demos.purpose: commands/tests/test_release_repair.py runs this lesson against lesson 11.2's stand-in gcloud, extended with the template, gcloud run services update, the service and revision lists, and a stand-in make for the smokes. Where a POSIX sh is installed, as in Cloud Shell, 2 of its tests run the Makefile's own recipes: the whole controlled failure from make promote-gated back to the gated state, including that a make release-candidate after the rollback inherits the typo, and make smoke-deployed itself, with its one HTTP request caught by a local proxy. It calls nothing in Google Cloud and costs nothing; it starts a process for every stand-in call, so give it a few minutes.

demos.heading: On your lane: promote, break it, roll back
demos.purpose: gate-check reads lesson 11.2's record, the files first and then the lane; when every check passes, make promote moves the traffic and prints what /version now says. make candidate makes a revision from the template, with every setting it passes at the Makefile's default except the one you name. It takes no traffic, gets the candidate tag and goes into .candidate-revision. The same gate as lesson 11.2's, on the revision the file now names: about ten minutes of rows, and every row that reaches the model fails. run_eval.py's lines stream between the gate's two blocks. The verdict is recorded, red, and make reports release.py's exit 1 on its last line, Error 1, before exiting 2 itself. First make promote-gated, which the red record stops at its first recipe line, line 46 of mk/release.mk, so its make promote never starts. Then plain make promote, which reads no record and moves all the traffic to the mistyped revision. Go straight on to the next cell. make smoke-deployed names the smokes it skips and runs the rest; make incident reads what the smokes logged, with the gate record and the lane. time is the shell's own: when the command ends, it prints how long it took. The manifest's proof for this lesson asks for under two minutes. Do it: the smokes and the incident, after the rollback The cell reads documind-api and its revisions from the Cloud Run Admin API's v1 resources, the same JSON gcloud run services describe --format=json prints, without release.py: each recent revision's traffic, tag, image and model, then the template's, and whether the template is what serves. Each revision's image is a digest and the template's a tag, so the cell compares the template through the revision it made last, as make incident does. Run it now, before the repair, while they differ.
